ideas.pitch: A Python-based static analysis and linting CLI tailored specifically for competitive programming snippets in C, C++, Java, and Python to spot common syntax and logical errors instantly.
ideas.title: BugHuntAI CLI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core skill tested in Round 1 of the competition (debugging buggy snippets without code execution).

ideas.pitch: An offline execution trace visualizer that maps out variable states step-by-step for C++ and Python data structures during complex algorithm problem solving.
ideas.title: AlgoTrace Visualizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses logical thinking and problem-solving metrics by making dry-runs visual, highly appealing for programming challenge judges.

ideas.pitch: A standalone extension that scans C/C++ and Python codebases to evaluate time and space complexity automatically, flagging suboptimal solutions before submission.
ideas.title: ComplexityMeter
ideas.why_it_could_win: Evaluates solutions directly on efficiency and correctness, which are the main judging criteria for Round 2.

ideas.pitch: A fast refactoring utility that takes messy, non-readable competitive programming code and formats it for readability and maintainability.
ideas.title: SnippetSanitizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targeted explicitly at readability and coding style, two vital pillars of the event's evaluation rubric.

ideas.pitch: An automated fuzz testing tool that generates tricky edge cases and boundary inputs for given algorithmic problem statements to stress-test candidate solutions.
ideas.title: EdgeCaseGenerator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Emphasizes deep programming concepts and logical thinking by challenging solutions with rigorous failure modes.
